Demo: edit a component, state-preserving hot reload against the live native tree in under a second.

M9 — Packaging + updates: `nd package` produces per-platform artifacts — macOS .app with hardened runtime, allow-jit entitlement (JSC under Bun requires it on Apple Silicon), deep-signing of nested binaries, notarytool + staple; Windows signed NSIS installer + winget manifest (Azure Artifact Signing documented as default cert path); Linux Flatpak manifest (GNOME 50 runtime) + AppImage for nightlies. Updates in the Zig core: minisign/Ed25519-verified manifests (non-disableable, Tauri-style) with zig-bsdiff+zstd deltas and full-download fallback. Demo: a signed, notarized, auto-updating release of the gallery app on all three platforms from one CI workflow.

M10 — Plugin system + security hardening: capability ACL enforced at the NDP dispatch layer (per-window grants, namespaced plugin permissions, ACL-driven command dead-code elimination), native plugin ABI with manifest-driven codegen, wasmtime/Extism sandbox tier for untrusted plugins, and the optional binary command-buffer fast path for large commits. Demo: a third-party WASM plugin adds a widget and a permission-gated command; an ACL-denied command fails loudly; 10k-node mount benchmark before/after the binary path.

proposals.name: NativeDesktop — platform architecture: libnd C-ABI core + NDP versioned protocol + React-to-native-widget backends
proposals.summary: NativeDesktop is built libghostty-style: a Zig 0.16.0 core library (libnd) with a stable, versioned C ABI that owns the retained widget tree, per-platform backend plugins (GTK4 via zig-gobject, AppKit via a thin Swift shell over a C vtable, Win32+Direct2D/DirectWrite custom Fluent widgets via zigwin32), and a versioned binary wire protocol (NDP) that decouples the React/TypeScript runtime from the core. Bun runs the app's React code against a vendored react@19.2 + react-reconciler@0.33 mutation-mode renderer that emits one batched command buffer per React commit; NDP travels over either a unix-socket/named-pipe transport (default: Zig host, Bun sidecar) or an in-process N-API/bun:ffi transport (Bun host, core as dylib) — the same abstraction a future CEF backend and non-Bun embedders slot into. The agent-first automation server (widget-tree dump with stable IDs, in-process screenshots, semantic input synthesis, headless CI support) lives inside the Zig core sharing the same node registry as the renderer, exposed as JSON-RPC plus a first-party MCP wrapper, so it works even when the JS runtime hangs. Extensibility is three-tier: TS plugins in Bun, untrusted plugins in wasmtime/Extism WASM behind a Tauri-v2-style capability ACL, and audited native plugins against the versioned C plugin ABI.
proposals.process_model: Default topology (Mode A, "host"): a small Zig host executable owns main() and runs the platform UI loop natively and blocking — GLib main context on Linux, NSApplication.run on the macOS main thread (satisfying AppKit's main-thread rule), the Win32 message pump on Windows — exactly the Ghostty pattern, avoiding any bet on integrating std.Io's event loop with toolkit loops (std.Io.Threaded is used only for core-internal I/O such as the automation socket and updater). The host spawns Bun 1.3.13 (pinned; revalidated on the 1.4.x Rust line later) as a child process running the React app; they speak NDP over a unix socket / named pipe with length-prefixed binary frames, because Bun.spawn's built-in ipc is Bun-to-Bun only. Crash isolation falls out: a JS crash leaves windows alive for the automation layer to inspect, and a hung JS runtime cannot block screenshots or tree dumps — a hard agent-first requirement. Cross-thread handoff inside the core uses g_main_context_invoke_full / dispatch_async_f / PostMessage, one closure per React commit, never per mutation. Optional topology (Mode B, "embedded"): Bun is the host executable and libnd loads as an N-API shared library (Bun's production-recommended native path; bun:ffi kept as an experimental fast lane), with JS and the UI loop cooperatively sharing Bun's main thread — offered for apps needing heavy synchronous measurement, and it doubles as the proof that libnd is embeddable by any C-ABI host. WASM plugins run in-process inside wasmtime instances; a future CEF backend brings its own multi-process model behind the same backend vtable. Automation server runs on a std.Io.Threaded worker inside the core process in both modes.
proposals.runtime_integration: The boundary is engine-agnostic by construction: libnd exports a flat C ABI (nd_session_create, nd_apply_ops(ptr,len), nd_drain_events, nd_measure_text, nd_snapshot_tree, versioned via an abi_version field in the init struct), and everything above it speaks NDP — a versioned, negotiated (hello/version-handshake), fixed-layout binary opcode stream with an interned-string table, not JSON (Electrobun's pre-v1 per-message JSON is the documented anti-pattern; a custom command buffer beats FlatBuffers/Protobuf for a transient ops stream). Mode A transport: length-prefixed NDP frames over unix socket/named pipe, ~2-6us per message, which is irrelevant at one frame per commit; a dedicated synchronous request-reply channel serves the rare blocking calls (text measurement for custom-drawn widgets, useLayoutEffect geometry reads), and the core proactively pushes computed geometry back after every commit so most layout reads hit a JS-side cache without a round trip. Mode B transport: the identical NDP buffer passed by pointer in a single N-API call per commit (zero-copy ArrayBuffer), with native-to-JS events in a native SPSC ring buffer drained once per JS tick — never JSCallback from GUI threads (oven-sh/bun#15925, leak reports on #7582). Explicitly rejected: linking Bun's Zig internals (dead — Bun's core is Rust as of May 2026, no libbun per oven-sh/bun#12017) and building the core protocol on bun:ffi alone (officially experimental). Fallback if Bun becomes untenable: embed JavaScriptCore directly (proven from Zig) or quickjs-ng for the scripting tier — the NDP boundary makes either a runtime swap, not a rewrite.
proposals.renderer_design: TS side: react-reconciler@0.33.0 in MUTATION mode (native toolkits are mutable retained trees), vendored/bundled together with react@19.2.x inside the framework package exactly as react-three-fiber v9.5 does — the reconciler breaks on React minors ('resolveUpdatePriority is not a function' on 19.1→19.2), so app React versions never float against it. Render-phase host config methods (createInstance, appendInitialChild) build cheap JS descriptors only — concurrent rendering can discard uncommitted trees, and allocating GTK/NSView objects there would leak natives. At commitMutationEffects time the renderer serializes the mutation set (CREATE, INSERT, REMOVE, UPDATE-diffed-in-commitUpdate since prepareUpdate is gone, SET_TEXT, SHOW/HIDE) into a growable ArrayBuffer keyed by monotonically assigned, generation-tagged stable node IDs, then crosses the boundary exactly once per commit. The Zig core applies the buffer on the UI thread inside a frame-aligned callback (gtk_widget_add_tick_callback on Linux; CVDisplayLink/main-queue dispatch on macOS) into its authoritative retained tree — Fabric's shadow-tree idea, and that same tree is the automation layer's dump source and input-addressing scheme. Events flow back priority-tagged (discrete never dropped, continuous coalesced keep-latest, per Fabric), and the resolveUpdatePriority/getCurrentUpdatePriority family maps native event classes to Discrete/Continuous/DefaultEventPriority so startTransition works. hideInstance/unhideInstance map to gtk_widget_set_visible / NSView.isHidden / ShowWindow so Suspense fallbacks hide without unmounting. getRootHostContext/getChildHostContext return non-null sentinels (React 19 requirement). React Compiler 1.0 ships in the default template (renderer-agnostic, cuts commit traffic). Fast Refresh: react-refresh via setRefreshHandler, bundled in the same chunk as the reconciler; generation-tagged IDs let the core garbage-collect orphaned generations on hot reload instead of leaking widgets.
proposals.layout_and_widgets: Widget layer contract: a platform-neutral widget schema (~30 core widgets: Window, Box, Grid, Button, Label, TextInput, Checkbox, Slider, List, Menu, TabView, Image, ScrollView, ...) defined as machine-readable metadata from which ALL bindings and TS types are code-generated — hand-written bindings are the documented cause of death for Proton Native/React-NodeGui/Yue. Sources: GObject-Introspection GIR drives zig-gobject (master, post-April-2026 for Zig 0.16) on Linux and also feeds the TS-facing metadata; win32metadata drives zigwin32 on Windows; the macOS backend is a thin Swift/AppKit shell (Ghostty pattern) implementing the same C backend vtable, with zig-objc reserved for small in-core needs. Layout: delegate to the platform — Box/Grid map to GtkBox/GtkGrid with hexpand/vexpand on Linux and to manual setFrame layout computed by a shared Zig Box/Grid engine on macOS (isFlipped=true containers, never Auto Layout mixed with computed frames) and Windows (custom-drawn widgets need it anyway); no Yoga port unless a custom-drawn layer later justifies it. Missing-widget strategy, three tiers per widget per platform: (1) map to a real native widget; (2) compose from native primitives; (3) custom-drawn fallback (Direct2D/DirectWrite on Windows — the default there, since stock common controls are Windows-8-era and dark-mode-hostile; GskRenderNode/Cairo on Linux; custom NSView/CALayer on macOS), with every custom-drawn widget getting accessibility via AccessKit's C bindings (already GTK 4.18's own Windows/macOS a11y backend) and a UIA provider + AutomationId on Windows from day one. Styling is an explicit constrained style-prop system — never a web-CSS promise: props compile to widget properties plus a GtkCssProvider dialect on Linux, appearance/attribute setters on macOS, Fluent design tokens for the Direct2D theme on Windows; the core validates styles against each backend's actual property set and returns loud structured errors over NDP, because LLM agents reliably hallucinate flexbox into GTK CSS. Scalable lists map to GtkListView + GtkSignalListItemFactory recycling, with the React item-template mechanism binding rows on demand.
proposals.extensibility: Everything above libnd is a plugin against a versioned surface. (1) Backend plugins: each UI backend (GTK4, AppKit, Win32/D2D, later CEF or a webview) implements a C vtable — create/destroy/reparent widget, set property, run loop hooks, snapshot, dispatch-semantic-action, measure — negotiated by abi_version; a CEF backend later maps NDP widget ops to DOM/browser-shell surfaces and brings its own process model without touching the renderer or protocol, which is why NDP stays transport- and backend-neutral. (2) TS plugins: ordinary npm packages running in Bun (or Bun Workers for isolation), calling framework APIs that are themselves NDP commands; Bun's default lifecycle-script blocking (trustedDependencies) is preserved and lockfile+audit enforced in the CLI build path against Shai-Hulud-class supply-chain attacks. (3) Zig/native plugins: dylibs implementing a semver'd C plugin ABI (nd_plugin_v1 struct with abi_version, capability declarations, init/deinit), reserved for first-party/audited code, deep-signed with JIT entitlements on macOS. (4) Untrusted third-party plugins: wasmtime via Extism, WASI capability-scoped, with a deliberately minimal host-function surface (2026 wasmtime CVEs show the sandbox is only as strong as the host API). All plugin and window commands pass a Tauri-v2-style capability ACL enforced at the NDP boundary in the Zig core — per-window, namespaced ${plugin}:${permission} grants that double as a dead-code-elimination manifest. Embeddability: libnd itself is consumable by non-Bun hosts (Swift app, Rust app, test harness) exactly like libghostty, because the renderer only ever talks NDP.
risks: Bun dependency instability: the Zig lineage died at 1.3.14 and the Rust 1.4.x line will regress (a July 2026 regression already broke bun:ffi dlopen in --compile builds); mitigated by pinning, the engine-agnostic NDP boundary, and a JavaScriptCore/quickjs-ng fallback plan, but revalidation cost per Bun release is real.

react-reconciler has no semver and breaks on React MINOR releases; vendoring the react+reconciler pair contains the blast radius but makes every React upgrade a scheduled migration project with no official host-config docs.

Zig churn: 0.17 (~Aug 2026) reworks the build system months after we adopt 0.16, and the no-AI-contribution policy means toolchain bugs must be patched locally; mitigated by the Ghostty/TigerBeetle pin-and-migrate discipline and thin centralized build.zig logic.

Windows is the known hard case: Microsoft itself retreated from native XAML widget trees to composition-plus-islands, so our custom-drawn Direct2D/DirectWrite Fluent widget set plus per-widget UIA providers is the single largest engineering line item and the most likely schedule-breaker.

Widget-breadth demand is the historical killer (Proton Native, React-NodeGui, Yue all died under 'add more components'); codegen from GIR/win32metadata mitigates tier 1, but tier-2 composed and tier-3 custom-drawn widgets are still hand-built per platform.

Mode A's synchronous measure/layout-read path over the socket (~tens of microseconds per round trip) may prove too slow for text-measure-heavy custom layouts, forcing Mode B (in-process) to become the de facto default and weakening the crash-isolation story.

In-process screenshots miss OS decorations, popovers/sheets on separate native surfaces, and externally composited content (future CEF, video); agents can act on misleading captures unless the snapshot API composites per-surface or labels the gap explicitly.

macOS distribution friction: hardened runtime + com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit for the Bun child, deep-signing every nested binary, and notarization are the most common failure pipeline; TCC-free in-process automation avoids CI permission walls but sign/notarize automation must work from the first release.
milestones: M1 — Toolchain + blank window (Linux): repo with exact-pinned Zig 0.16.0 and Bun 1.3.13 (Nix flake / vendored downloads, Ghostty-style), libnd skeleton exporting nd_session_create over C ABI, Zig host binary opening a blank GTK 4.22 window via zig-gobject (pinned post-April-2026 master commit); CI job proves it under weston --backend=headless with GSK_RENDERER=cairo. Demo: ./nd-host opens a window locally and passes headless CI.

M2 — NDP v0 + Bun sidecar: versioned handshake and length-prefixed binary frames over a unix socket; Zig host spawns Bun child; a TS script creates a window, sets its title, and receives a close event. Demo: `nd dev hello.ts` shows a live TS-driven native window; protocol version mismatch fails loudly.

M3 — React renderer MVP: vendored react@19.2 + react-reconciler@0.33 mutation-mode renderer with per-commit command buffers, generation-tagged node IDs, and priority-tagged event drain; 8 hand-mapped GTK widgets (Window, Box, Button, Label, TextInput, Checkbox, Image, ScrollView). Demo: a TSX counter app with working onClick, setState, Suspense fallback via hide/unhide, and startTransition.

M4 — Agent automation layer v1: JSON-RPC server in libnd behind NATIVE_AUTOMATION=1 (local WebSocket + stdio), exposing getTree (stable refs = node ID + testID prop, roles, names, geometry with explicit logical-vs-pixel coordinate space), screenshot via gsk_renderer_render_texture -> PNG, semantic click/type/setValue with actionability hit-tests, waitFor; first-party MCP wrapper; raw screenshot+coordinate surface for Anthropic computer-use loops. Demo: Claude Code drives the M3 counter app headless in CI via MCP with zero OS permissions.

M5 — Codegen + widget breadth + styling (Linux): GIR-driven metadata pipeline generating Zig glue and TS component types for ~30 core widgets including GtkListView virtualized lists via GtkSignalListItemFactory; constrained style-prop system compiling to widget props + GtkCssProvider with loud validation errors over NDP. Demo: a settings-page gallery app with a 100k-row list scrolling at 60fps, built partly by an agent using M4.

M6 — macOS backend: Swift/AppKit shell library implementing the backend C vtable (linked into libnd, SwiftPM-built), NSApplication on the main thread, shared Zig Box/Grid layout via setFrame with isFlipped containers, NSView.cacheDisplay screenshots, NSApplication.postEvent + semantic AX-style actions, setAccessibilityIdentifier mirroring; sign/notarize/staple (notarytool) automated in the CLI with allow-jit entitlements. Demo: the M5 gallery app runs unmodified on macOS and the M4 MCP tools drive it on a stock GitHub Actions macOS runner.

M7 — Mode B in-process embedding + HMR: libnd compiled as an N-API dylib loaded by Bun-as-host (bun:ffi fast path behind a flag), same NDP buffer via one applyOps(ptr,len) per commit, SPSC event ring drained per tick, cooperative loop pumping; react-refresh wired through setRefreshHandler with generation-GC of orphaned native nodes. Demo: `nd dev --hot` edits TSX and the live native window updates without losing widget state; the same app binary also runs in Mode A.

M8 — Windows backend: zigwin32 Win32 windowing with per-monitor-v2 DPI and WM_DPICHANGED handling, custom-drawn Fluent widget set on Direct2D/DirectWrite implementing the shared Box/Grid layout, every widget shipping a UIA provider with AutomationId (this IS the automation layer on Windows), PrintWindow/PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT screenshots with Windows.Graphics.Capture fallback, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE plus version-gated uxtheme ordinals. Demo: gallery app + MCP-driven test run on a GitHub Actions Windows runner.

M9 — Plugin system + capability ACL: versioned nd_plugin_v1 C ABI for native plugins, TS plugin packages, wasmtime/Extism sandbox for untrusted plugins with WASI-scoped capabilities, and Tauri-v2-style per-window/per-plugin command allowlists enforced at the NDP boundary (doubling as dead-code-elimination manifest); backend-vtable conformance suite plus a spike 'null backend' proving a second backend (CEF-shaped) slots in without renderer changes. Demo: a third-party WASM plugin adds a menu item but is denied filesystem access by the ACL, visibly and loudly.

M10 — Packaging + updates: `nd build` produces Flatpak (portal-aware) + AppImage on Linux, deep-signed notarized stapled .app on macOS, signed NSIS installer + winget manifest on Windows (Azure Artifact Signing documented as the default cert path); minisign/Ed25519-verified update manifests (non-disableable) with zig-bsdiff+zstd delta patches and full-artifact fallback, updater implemented in libnd. Demo: a released gallery app self-updates from vN to vN+1 via a delta patch on all three platforms.

scores.name: Proposal 1 (Hotline — in-process Bun host + bun:ffi)
scores.note: Front-loads the least-proven mechanism as its foundation: M2 depends on cooperatively pumping GTK/NSApp from Bun's tick, when the research explicitly says Bun exposes no event-loop pumping API and run-loop interleaving is fragile — the proposal itself admits this is 'the least-proven piece' and keeps a sidecar fallback 'reachable', which is a topology rewrite disguised as a mitigation. Builds the default hot path on bun:ffi (officially experimental, dlopen regression #30717 already hit --compile) and mitigates by maintaining TWO binding layers (bun:ffi + N-API) with per-commit conformance tests — that's doubled binding maintenance for a small team. M1 also spans Linux AND macOS on day one. The renderer, command buffer, and codegen thinking are excellent, but M1-M3 carry the highest probability of a forced mid-project pivot.

scores.name: Proposal 2 (two-process Zig host + Bun child, JSON NDP)
scores.note: Best aligned with every flagged gotcha for M1-M3: Zig owns main() and blocks in the native loop (no Bun pumping bet), no bun:ffi anywhere on the core path, no Bun.spawn ipc, only stable Bun features (spawn, sockets, bundler). Length-prefixed JSON batched per commit is deliberately boring — cheapest to build, debug, and demo, with the binary buffer as a contained later optimization behind the same op list. Milestones are the smallest and most incremental (Linux-only through M5, kill -9 crash-isolation demo at M2). Honest about its two soft spots: the ~10-50us sync measurement round-trip ('rare by construction' is a mild hand-wave — text-heavy lists could bite) and 10k-node JSON mounts. The fs.readSync-on-socket-fd sync channel is under-specified for the Windows named-pipe case, but that's an M7 problem.

scores.name: Proposal 3 (libnd — dual Mode A/B, versioned binary NDP)
scores.note: Same sound topology as Proposal 2 (Zig host owns the loop, Ghostty pattern) and the best long-term architecture (versioned handshake, abi_version'd C ABI, backend vtable, headless CI in M1). But it buys that generality with up-front machinery a small team must build before the first useful demo: binary fixed-layout protocol with interned strings and version negotiation at M2, plus a second full topology (Mode B in-process) at M7 that quietly re-imports Proposal 1's cooperative-pumping risk in one clause without addressing it. The 'core proactively pushes computed geometry so layout reads hit a JS cache' claim hand-waves the hard part — geometry only exists after allocate, and useLayoutEffect reads are synchronous, so cache-miss semantics are unspecified. Dual modes plus a CEF-shaped null backend is speculative surface area for a team of this size.

verdicts.rationale: Through a strict feasibility-and-effort lens for milestones 1-3, Proposal 2 wins because every early milestone rests only on proven, stable ground: Zig owns main() and runs the native loop blocking (exactly what the research prescribes, avoiding the undemonstrated Bun-tick pumping entirely), the transport is stable-Bun-features-only (child process + unix socket), and the wire format is deliberately dumb JSON batched once per React commit — which the research confirms is fine at that batching granularity. Its M1 (GTK window from Zig), M2 (protocol + kill-9-survivable Bun child), and M3 (React renderer) are the smallest, most independently demoable increments of the three, and each de-risks exactly one thing. Proposal 1 inverts this: its M2 gates the entire project on cooperative main-loop pumping that the research flags as fragile and that nobody ships at scale, while building the default binding on experimental bun:ffi and paying for the hedge with a permanently doubled binding layer — for a small team that is the highest-variance path, and its own 'fallback to Zig-host + Bun-sidecar' escape hatch concedes that Proposal 2's topology is the safe one. Proposal 3 shares Proposal 2's sound topology and is arguably the best end-state architecture, but it front-loads versioned binary protocol machinery, an abi-versioned vtable abstraction, and eventually a second topology (Mode B) — abstraction tax paid before any user-visible value, and its dual-mode maintenance burden plus the hand-waved geometry-cache story make it meaningfully more expensive for the same M1-M3 outcome. On immature-dependency penalties: all three correctly pin Bun 1.3.13 and post-April zig-gobject master, but only Proposal 1 places an experimental dependency (bun:ffi) and an unproven integration pattern on its critical path.
graft: From Proposal 3: add the NDP version handshake (hello + version negotiation, abi_version field) to Proposal 2's protocol at M2 — it costs a day now and makes the later JSON-to-binary migration and any non-Bun runtime adapter negotiable instead of a flag day.
From Proposal 3: pull the headless-CI proof (weston --backend=headless + GSK_RENDERER=cairo) forward from Proposal 2's M4 into M1, so the CI story is validated before anything is built on top of it.

From Proposals 1/3: adopt the in-process N-API 'Mode B-lite' as a targeted fix for Proposal 2's weakest spot — an optional N-API module exposing only nd_measure_text/geometry reads gives sub-microsecond synchronous measurement for text-heavy apps without abandoning the two-process default or touching bun:ffi.

From Proposal 1: write the fixed-layout binary command-buffer spec (opcode u8, generation-tagged u32 node IDs, interned string table) as a schema document during M3 even while shipping JSON, keeping the JSON and binary encodings 1:1 over the same op list so the optimization stays a drop-in.
From Proposal 3: build the 'null backend' conformance suite against the widget schema early, so GTK behavior is pinned by tests before the macOS and Windows backends are written against it.

From Proposal 1: the event-drain design detail of mapping priority tags directly onto react-reconciler's DiscreteEventPriority/ContinuousEventPriority lanes, plus its explicit SPSC coalescing rules (discrete never dropped, continuous keep-latest) — Proposal 2 gestures at this but Proposal 1 specifies it precisely enough to implement.

scores.name: Proposal 1 — Hotline (in-process Bun host + Zig dylib)
scores.note: Best raw hot path: zero-copy command buffer over ~2ns bun:ffi, truly synchronous microsecond nd_measure_text, SPSC pull-based event ring with Fabric-style priority coalescing, vsync-aligned apply via frame-clock tick/CVDisplayLink. But the entire architecture stands on its least-proven piece: cooperative pumping of GTK/NSApp/PeekMessage from Bun's tick — nobody ships that at scale on macOS, and it puts JS execution, GC pauses, and UI painting on one contended thread, so a long JS task or GC pause directly eats the 16ms frame budget. 60fps under heavy JS load is structurally worse than a host-owned UI thread, and the fallback topology is 'reachable' but unbuilt.

scores.name: Proposal 2 — two-process Zig host + JSON NDP
scores.note: Best UI-thread discipline of the three (blocking native loop, JS crashes/GC never stall painting, one closure per commit) and correct event coalescing/priority model. But it puts length-prefixed JSON on the hot path and defers the binary buffer to M10 — the research explicitly says batched binary is the fix, not faster JSON; 10k-node mounts are an admitted soft spot. Worse, synchronous measurement/useLayoutEffect reads block on a 10-50us IPC round trip via fs.readSync with no caching mitigation — a text-heavy layout pass or layout-effect-heavy commit multiplies that into milliseconds. Sound skeleton, weakest hot path.

scores.name: Proposal 3 — libnd C-ABI core + versioned binary NDP, dual-mode
scores.note: Combines the proven topology (Mode A: Zig host owns main() and a blocking native loop — Ghostty pattern, zero pump risk, JS/GC isolated from the UI thread) with a binary fixed-layout command buffer plus interned strings from day one. The sync-read problem gets two real mitigations: proactive geometry push-back after every commit so most layout reads hit a JS-side cache, and Mode B (in-process N-API, same buffer by pointer, SPSC ring drain) as the documented path for measure-heavy apps. Frame-aligned apply, priority-tagged coalesced events, generation-GC of orphaned nodes, no JSCallback from GUI threads — every hot-path gotcha is addressed. Costs: dual-mode doubles transport testing surface, and Mode B's cooperative pump is under-specified relative to Proposal 1's.

verdicts.winner: Proposal 3 — libnd C-ABI core + versioned binary NDP, dual-mode
verdicts.rationale: Through a pure performance-and-soundness lens, the decisive questions are: (1) does the UI thread ever wait on JS, (2) is the per-commit bridge binary and single-crossing, and (3) can synchronous measure/useLayoutEffect reads be served inside the frame budget. Proposal 3 is the only one that answers all three without betting on unproven machinery. Its default Mode A keeps the platform loop native and blocking (the Ghostty pattern that is known to work), so GC pauses and long JS tasks degrade app logic latency but never scroll, animation, or paint — the strongest 60fps-under-load posture. Its wire format is a fixed-layout binary opcode stream with interned strings from day one, exactly one crossing per React commit in both transports, which is the documented fix for bridge overhead; Proposal 2 ships JSON on the hot path and admits large mounts are a soft spot until M10. For the synchronous-read hazard, Proposal 3 layers a post-commit geometry push (making most layout reads a JS-side cache hit) under an in-process Mode B escape hatch with true sync FFI measure — whereas Proposal 2 eats a 10-50us blocking IPC round trip per read, and Proposal 1 gets microsecond measure only by accepting the single-process topology everywhere. Proposal 1 is genuinely excellent on the hot path — arguably the fastest steady-state bridge — but its foundation is cooperative pumping of NSApp/GLib from Bun's tick as the only topology, which the research flags as fragile and unshipped at scale on macOS, and which co-locates JS execution, JS GC, and UI painting on one thread. Since all three proposals delegate layout to native containers (shrinking the sync-measure advantage that most favors in-process), Proposal 1's residual edge no longer justifies its structural risk. Proposal 3 gets ~90% of Proposal 1's bridge performance in Mode B when needed, while defaulting to the topology with the best worst-case frame behavior, a versioned ABI, and a clean memory model (Zig-owned retained tree, generation-tagged IDs, commit-only native allocation) on both sides of the GC/manual boundary.
graft: Proposal 1's concrete cooperative-pump spec should become Mode B's design doc: fd-wakeup-integrated g_main_context_iteration(ctx, FALSE) (never busy-polled), manual NSApp event pumping on Bun's main thread, PeekMessage draining on Windows — plus its explicit fallback criteria for when to abandon in-process mode.

Proposal 1's twin-binding conformance suite: bind the identical C header via both bun:ffi and an N-API addon and run the same test matrix against both in CI every commit, so the experimental bun:ffi fast lane can never silently diverge from the stable fallback.

Proposal 1's per-platform vsync-aligned apply detail: land mutation batches inside gtk_widget_add_tick_callback on Linux, CVDisplayLink-aligned drain on macOS, DWM-synced apply on Windows, so ops always commit before layout and paint of the same frame.

Proposal 2's NDP_TRACE=1 mode: pretty-print every binary frame per commit for human/agent debugging — binary protocols lose JSON's greppability, so build the tracer into the protocol layer from M2, not later.

Proposal 2's crash-isolation demos as regression tests: kill -9 the Bun child with the window surviving, plus the host-rendered in-window error overlay when the JS runtime dies — these prove Mode A's isolation payoff is real, not theoretical.

Proposal 2's lint/docs treatment of synchronous reads: statically flag useLayoutEffect geometry reads and sync measure calls as slow-path in Mode A, with the fix-it suggesting the cached-geometry API or Mode B — and gate the binary-buffer hot path with Proposal 2's 10k-node mount benchmark as a permanent perf regression test.

scores.name: Proposal 1 (Hotline — in-process Bun host + Zig dylib)
scores.note: Best raw in-process DX (sub-microsecond nd_measure_text, lowest-latency HMR, single debugger target) and the manifest-codegen TS-types story is solid. But its longevity is the weakest through this lens: Bun is the host executable and the cooperative GTK/NSApp/PeekMessage pump lives inside Bun's tick — self-described as 'least-proven, especially on macOS'. The C ABI is engine-agnostic but the process topology is not: swapping runtimes after a Bun 1.4 fiasco means also re-owning the main loop, which is exactly the coupling the research gotchas warn about. A 4th backend fares worst here too — CEF's own multi-process model plus CefDoMessageLoopWork would be a third loop stacked on an already fragile pump, and the 'foreign-surface leaf widget' answer treats CEF as an embedded surface rather than a peer backend. Community native modules load in-process, inheriting macOS deep-sign/JIT-entitlement burden and zero crash isolation.

scores.name: Proposal 2 (Zig host + Bun child, JSON NDP)
scores.note: Best day-one developer experience of the three: NDP_TRACE=1 greppable JSON frames, a host that survives kill -9 of the Bun child (windows stay up, agent can screenshot the frozen app), a host-rendered in-window error overlay on JS crash, and an explicit milestone (M8) shipping current-idiom Zig/GTK agent docs — the only proposal that budgets for the LLM-hallucination gotchas as a deliverable. Engine-agnostic socket boundary is real, not aspirational: any runtime that speaks NDP attaches, which is the right hedge for Bun's Rust-rewrite churn. Weaknesses through this lens: JSON per-commit is a known soft spot for 10k-node mounts (binary path deferred to M10), sync measurement at 10-50us over IPC is a permanent useLayoutEffect tax with no in-process escape hatch, and the plugin/backend surfaces are described but not formally versioned — 'metadata manifest' vs Proposal 3's semver'd ABI structs.

scores.name: Proposal 3 (libnd + versioned NDP + backend vtable, dual mode)
scores.note: Strongest on exactly the longevity questions in the lens. The 4th-backend question has a concrete engineering answer, not a paragraph of hope: backends implement an abi_version-negotiated C vtable, and M9 ships a conformance suite plus a 'null backend' spike proving a CEF-shaped backend slots in without renderer or protocol changes. Community native modules get the only semver'd contract (nd_plugin_v1 with capability declarations), and TS types for plugin widgets flow from the same codegen pipeline. The Bun-death hedge is double: engine-agnostic versioned NDP with a handshake, plus a named JSC/quickjs-ng fallback. Mode B (in-process N-API) recovers Proposal 1's fast-sync-measure DX for apps that need it, and the geometry push-back cache kills most sync round trips in Mode A. Costs: dual-mode is real ongoing maintenance surface, binary-from-day-one loses Proposal 2's greppable debugging unless a trace decoder is added, and HMR lands at M7 — later than ideal for a DX-first pitch.

verdicts.winner: Proposal 3 (libnd C-ABI core + versioned NDP + backend vtable)
verdicts.rationale:
Through the developer-experience-and-longevity lens, the three proposals are near-identical on React DX fundamentals — all vendor react@19.2 + react-reconciler@0.33 r3f-style, all do descriptor-only render phase with commit-time widget allocation, all wire react-refresh with generation-tagged GC, all codegen TS types from a widget schema, all copy the Tauri v2 capability ACL. So the decision comes down to the two questions the lens weights hardest: does the design survive a 4th backend, and does it survive community native modules and runtime churn.

Proposal 3 is the only one that answers both with versioned, testable contracts rather than prose. The backend vtable with abi_version negotiation plus the M9 null-backend conformance spike is a falsifiable claim that a CEF/webview backend slots in without touching the renderer or protocol; Proposal 2 merely argues its process tree can accommodate CEF, and Proposal 1's foreign-surface leaf widget is a webview-as-widget answer, not a backend answer — and any 4th backend in Proposal 1 must live inside the cooperative Bun-tick pump, its own self-declared least-proven component. For community native modules, Proposal 3's semver'd nd_plugin_v1 struct with capability declarations is the only plugin ABI a third-party author can build against across framework releases. For runtime longevity, the research is blunt that Bun 1.3.x is a dead lineage and the boundary must be engine-agnostic from day one: Proposal 1's boundary is engine-agnostic but its topology (Bun owns main() and the UI pump) is not; Proposals 2 and 3 both pass, and Proposal 3's versioned handshake plus dual-mode transport passes hardest, while Mode B claws back the synchronous-measurement DX that is Proposal 2's one permanent structural weakness (10-50us IPC measure calls with no escape hatch).

Proposal 2 loses narrowly, and only because its excellent DX affordances (JSON tracing, crash-surviving host, error overlay, agent-docs milestone) are all graftable onto Proposal 3's stronger skeleton, whereas Proposal 3's versioned ABI discipline cannot be retrofitted onto Proposal 2 late without breaking early adopters — retrofitting versioning is exactly the kind of platform debt that kills frameworks in year two. The main watch-item on the winner is dual-mode scope creep: Mode B should stay a conformance proof and measurement escape hatch, not a co-equal first-class topology, or it will double the support matrix.
